segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, thanks for making time, Dana. I wanted to confirm the rollout plan and the commercial piece for the 48 seats we discussed.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Sure. We’re still targeting May 6 for go-live. I just need the final quote to match 42 standard users and 6 admin users, not 50 total.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Got it. I updated that in the CRM this morning. The annual total comes to $38,640 before tax, with the onboarding package at $4,200 one-time.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay, that lines up. Can you also make sure billing starts June 1? Finance doesn’t want an invoice hitting before the new cost center opens.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yes, so I’ll set the contract start date as June 1, but we can still start implementation the week of April 22 under the order form.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That works. What are you assuming for onboarding hours?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: It includes 12 hours: two admin sessions, one manager training, and configuration support for the usage reports. If you need more, it’s $175 an hour, but most teams your size stay within the package.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay. Legal had one question on the renewal term. We need one-year renewal, not auto-renewing for two years.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: No problem. I’ll mark it as annual renewal with 60 days’ notice. Deal desk already approved that, so it won’t slow anything down.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Great. Send the revised order form today, and I’ll route it for signature. If procurement doesn’t have comments, we should be done by Friday.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Perfect. I’ll send it by 3 p.m. Eastern with the seat breakdown, June 1 billing date, and the one-year renewal language called out.
